english.title: Disclose information that a person has assumed a new identity - SOCA 2005

additionalkeywords.additionalkeyword: Serious Organised Crime and Police Act 2005

english.standardoffencewording: On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..),knowing or suspecting that a person was or had been a protected person and had assumed a new identity in pursuance of arrangements made under section 82(1) Serious Organised Crime and Police Act 2005, disclosed information which indicated that that person had assumed or might have assumed a new identity
english.legislation: Contrary to section 88(2) and (3) of the Serious Organised Crime and Police Act 2005.

english.notes:
(i) Section 89 of the Serious Organised Crime and Police Act 2005 provides defences in relation to the above offence:-
89(1) - not applicable to this offence.
89(2) D is not guilty of an offence under section 88(2) if-
(a) D disclosed the information with the agreement of P, and (b) at the time when D disclosed the information, it was not likely that its disclosure would endanger the safety of any person.
89(3) D is not guilty of an offence under section 88(2) if he disclosed the information for the purposes of safeguarding national security or for the purposes of the prevention, detection or investigation of crime.
89(4) D is not guilty of an offence under section 88(2) if-
(a) at the time when he disclosed the information, he was a protection provider or involved in the making of arrangements under section 82(1) or in the implementation, variation or cancellation of such arrangements, and (b) he disclosed the information for the purposes of the making, implementation, variation or cancellation of such arrangements.
89(6) Not applicable.
89(7) If sufficient evidence is adduced to raise an issue with respect to a defence under or by virtue of this section, the court or jury must assume that the defence is satisfied unless the prosecution proves beyond reasonable doubt that it is not.

other.penalty:
SUMMARY: Twelve months imprisonment and/or a fine not exceeding the statutory maximum.
INDICTMENT: Two years imprisonment and/or a fine

Until the commencement of section 282 of the Criminal Justice Act 2003 the penalty on summary conviction will be - Six months imprisonment and / or a fine not exceeding the statutory maximum

Time limit for prosecutions:
None

On the 12th March 2015 the limit on fines imposed by a Magistrates’ court was removed – as such, the potential fine on summary conviction in relation to an offence committed after this date is unlimited.
